title: Opposing Two Pointers
summary: Use one pointer at each end of ordered data and discard one side after each comparison when order proves that side cannot contain a better candidate.
recognition_signals: a pair or boundary relation depends on both ends
one comparison can rule out all candidates involving one boundary
core_rules: Move only the boundary whose current value makes the target impossible on that side.
Each move must discard candidates that are proven unnecessary by the ordering.
structural_steps: evaluate the current pair or boundary relation
return or record a match when appropriate
move the side that can be safely discarded

common_confusions.distinction: Opposing pointers usually discard from the two ends of an ordered candidate space. A variable window maintains one contiguous active range while the right side expands and the left side repairs validity.
